summary.text: Marianne Buttenschon represents the 119th Assembly District, which includes the cities of Utica and Rome and the communities of Floyd, Marcy, Whitestown and Deerfield.
Her official biography says she was previously Dean of Public Service and Emergency Preparedness at Mohawk Valley Community College and chairs the Assembly's Committee on Export Trade.

paragraphs.text: Buttenschon's 2018 campaign for the Assembly was her first attempt at elected office, according to her biography.

She earned an associate degree from Mohawk Valley Community College, a bachelor's degree in public justice from SUNY Polytechnic Institute, a master's degree in public policy from Binghamton University and a doctorate in education from Northeastern.
She and her husband, Don, have operated the Buttenschon Christmas Tree Farm in Marcy for over 30 years, and they have three children and six grandchildren.
In the Assembly she serves on the Agriculture, Banks, Economic Development, Education, Higher Education and Veterans Affairs committees.
Speaker Carl E. Heastie chose her as the Assembly's representative on the Interoperable and Emergency Communications Board, the biography says.
She is vice president of the Utica Community Food Pantry and belongs to the League of Women Voters, among other organizations.
